title: What can you say about DIM in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for DIM; the strongest is "Helps support healthy estrogen metabolism" (moderate, 60-200 mg a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Prevents or treats breast, prostate or cervical cancer".

supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 60-200 mg a day; no other listed source covers DIM.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada asks for a practitioner's advice before use, to rule out a serious cause of hormonal imbalance.

supported_wordings.wording: Provides an antioxidant that helps protect cells against damage from free radicals.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada sets a maximum dose only; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; Health Canada sets a maximum of 200 mg a day.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Prevents or treats breast, prostate or cervical cancer
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases; no listed source supports it.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats estrogen dominance, PCOS or endometriosis
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names or implies hormonal disorders. Health Canada asks for a practitioner's advice before use, to rule out a serious cause of hormonal imbalance.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Blocks estrogen like an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
